statement: Give the retrospective a portfolio scope so the outer loop can actually run: pooled cross-goal evidence for policy findings, and an explicit method-invention mandate — the retro may propose better procedures (brief shapes, delegation patterns, its own analysis steps), not just parameter tuning, grounded in disposition notes and PR bodies.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The first real portfolio retro runs on this repo's ledger and produces a cited, policy-artifacts-only proposal PR

backlog.title: ledger --all + two-scope retro.md with a method-invention mandate
backlog.detail: (1) goal-companion ledger gains --all: aggregate entries across every goal in the project (each entry already carries its slug; render with a [slug] prefix), refuse --all with a slug positional, refuse when no goals exist. (2) retro.md becomes two-scope: per-goal (process retro at close; floor 5 dispositions within the goal; below the global bar proposes goal-local hygiene only) and portfolio (ledger --all; policy retro; floor 5 dispositions machine-wide; the report MUST group findings by goal to expose task-type heterogeneity and MUST state the per-machine-per-project caveat). (3) Method-invention mandate, explicit: portfolio proposals may revise procedures encoded in policy artifacts — brief shapes, delegation patterns, choreography steps, retro.md itself — not only parameters; evidence comes from disposition notes and merged PR bodies, cited per finding. The policy-artifacts-only and never-auto-applied rails are unchanged. (4) Pins updated/extended in goal-docs.test.mjs; ledger --all tests in goal-companion.test.mjs.

disposition.notes: Direct implementation; two-scope split motivated by three live floor refusals at 1/4/2 dispositions against 7 machine-wide
